proposed.text: Why is FLAR often a more restrictive constraint than BHL in dense commercial zones?

options.text: Because FLAR limits the total GFA relative to lot size, preventing excessive building density even if height allows it.
Because commercial buildings are always wider than residential, so FLAR penalizes them by restricting the allowable floor area
Because BHL is measured from curb, while FLAR is measured from property line, affecting the overall building footprint
Because FLAR applies only in zones with high PSO%, limiting the potential for vertical expansion

proposed.rationale: PD 1096 supports the AMBF, PSO, FLAR, BHL, and TGFA workflow. Exact zoning values are local ordinance or problem-stated inputs, so the explanation should show the formula and avoid presenting practice-review values as universal code.
